title: Disk Space Monitoring (Windows)
exclusions: Monitors free capacity reported by the Windows `LogicalDisk` performance object for each collected logical-volume instance. It excludes the aggregate `_Total` instance because that value can conceal a full volume, and it does not infer which files, directories, applications, users, VSS snapshots, database logs, or backup products consumed the space. It does not measure physical-disk health, I/O latency, queueing, inode-like filesystem metadata, Storage Spaces pool capacity, SAN thin-provisioning headroom, cloud-provider disk quotas, unmounted/offline volumes, or hosts and instances absent from the input. Optical, removable, recovery, temporary, cluster, and mount-point instances remain in scope unless an accountable owner places an exact, expiring exception; do not remove `HarddiskVolume*` or non-drive-letter instances globally because valid mount points can use those identities. This operational alert is not evidence of regulatory compliance and performs no cleanup, expansion, deletion, or remediation.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `UC-1.2.3 - Windows LogicalDisk Free Capacity` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, triggered rows, and dispositions; the effective `Splunk_TA_windows` version and `inputs.conf`; `btool` output for the `perfmon://LogicalDisk` stanza; representative raw `% Free Space` and `Free Megabytes` events; the expected-host/instance coverage report; dashboard exports; the exact revision of any `windows_disk_capacity_exceptions.csv`; and dated positive, negative, boundary, missing-counter, `_Total`, stale-source, and duplicate-input control results. Each finding should preserve the completed sample time, `host`, `instance`, free and used percentage points, free megabytes, severity, search revision, and owner disposition. These artifacts demonstrate the configured control and observed data; they do not by themselves prove complete Windows estate coverage or runtime validation by this documentation review.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index, create six `Perfmon:LogicalDisk`-shaped events for `host=win-disk-lab-01`, `instance=C:` in three consecutive one-minute buckets. In every bucket provide one `% Free Space` and one `Free Megabytes` event with numeric `Value`; use paired values `(14.0,14336)`, `(9.5,9728)`, and `(4.5,4608)`. Apply the production pipeline after the base search with fixed test time bounds. Expect exactly one latest row for `C:` with `free_pct=4.5`, `used_pct=95.5`, `free_mb=4608`, `severity=critical`, and `low_samples=3`. Also confirm that the warning and high samples count as low even though their labels differ.
controlTest.negativeScenario: In the same isolated harness, provide paired `C:` samples at `15.0`, `14.0`, and `15.0` percent free; three paired `D:` samples exactly at `15.0`; three paired `_Total` samples at `1.0`; and three `E:` percentage samples without matching `Free Megabytes` events. Expect zero rows: pressure is not sustained for `C:`, the strict warning boundary does not include `15.0`, `_Total` is excluded, and incomplete counter pairs are rejected. Repeat with three low `C:` samples separated by a missing minute and confirm the 120-second window-span gate prevents a result.

dataSources: Local Windows Performance Data Helper samples from `\LogicalDisk(*)\% Free Space` and `\LogicalDisk(*)\Free Megabytes`, collected every 60 seconds by a Windows Universal Forwarder using the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows `[perfmon://LogicalDisk]` input. This implementation uses event index `index=perfmon`, `sourcetype=Perfmon:LogicalDisk`, `mode=single`, and fields `_time`, `host`, `object`, `counter`, `instance`, and numeric `Value`. `% Free Space` is percentage points of usable volume space that is free; `Free Megabytes` is Windows' reported unallocated capacity in megabytes.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) on the Windows collection tier, with its parsing and search-time knowledge installed where required by the deployment topology.
spl:
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:LogicalDisk" counter IN ("% Free Space","Free Megabytes") earliest=-10m@m latest=-2m@m
| where isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(instance) AND instance!="_Total"
| eval sample_minute=_time-(_time%60), numeric_value=tonumber(Value)
| where isnotnull(numeric_value)
| eval free_pct_value=if(counter="% Free Space",numeric_value,null()), free_mb_value=if(counter="Free Megabytes",numeric_value,null())
| stats latest(free_pct_value) as free_pct latest(free_mb_value) as free_mb by host instance sample_minute
| where isnotnull(free_pct) AND isnotnull(free_mb) AND free_pct>=0 AND free_pct<=100 AND free_mb>=0
| eval used_pct=round(100-free_pct,2), severity=case(free_pct<5,"critical",free_pct<10,"high",free_pct<15,"warning",true(),"normal"), is_low=if(severity!="normal",1,0)
| sort 0 host instance sample_minute
| streamstats window=3 sum(is_low) as low_samples count as sample_count min(sample_minute) as window_start by host instance
| eventstats max(sample_minute) as latest_sample by host instance
| where sample_minute=latest_sample AND sample_count=3 AND low_samples=3 AND sample_minute-window_start<=120
| eval free_pct=round(free_pct,2), free_mb=round(free_mb,0)
| table latest_sample host instance free_pct used_pct free_mb severity low_samples
| sort 0 severity free_pct host instance
description: Detects a Windows logical volume that remains below the local free-capacity policy for three consecutive one-minute samples. It pairs the native `% Free Space` and `Free Megabytes` counters per host, volume instance, and minute; rejects `_Total`, incomplete pairs, invalid units, and sample gaps; and reports the latest percentage, absolute free capacity, and severity without claiming a root cause.
value: A full Windows system, application, database, or log volume can stop services, prevent updates and log writes, disrupt failover, and leave too little room for recovery. Per-volume persistence and explicit boundary handling provide operators with actionable lead time while avoiding fleet noise from aggregate totals, one-sample transients, and malformed counter data.
implementation: Enable the add-on's local `[perfmon://LogicalDisk]` input with `% Free Space` and `Free Megabytes`, `instances=*`, `interval=60`, `mode=single`, and `useEnglishOnly=true`; route events to `index=perfmon`. Verify per-volume values against Windows Performance Monitor or `Get-Counter`, then schedule the search every five minutes, trigger on any result, and throttle by `host,instance` while the condition remains open. Treat 15/10/5 percent free as reviewable warning/high/critical starting points rather than Microsoft- or Splunk-mandated constants.
visualization: Build a Windows storage-capacity row with latest single values for critical and high volumes, a table of `host`, `instance`, `free_pct`, `used_pct`, `free_mb`, `severity`, and source age, and a 24-hour line chart of free percentage split by host-volume. Add a fleet heat map for the lowest free percentage and separate panels for expected hosts with no recent LogicalDisk data, incomplete counter pairs, and active expiring exceptions. Drill down to both raw counters for the selected volume and to the Windows/storage runbook; never label a process or directory as the consumer from these counters alone.
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=t latest(Performance.storage_free_percent) as free_pct from datamodel=Performance.Storage where Performance.storage_free_percent=* earliest=-10m@m latest=-2m@m by _time span=1m Performance.dest Performance.mount
| rename Performance.dest as host Performance.mount as instance
| where isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(instance) AND instance!="_Total" AND free_pct>=0 AND free_pct<=100
| eval sample_minute=_time, used_pct=round(100-free_pct,2), severity=case(free_pct<5,"critical",free_pct<10,"high",free_pct<15,"warning",true(),"normal"), is_low=if(severity!="normal",1,0)
| sort 0 host instance sample_minute
| streamstats window=3 sum(is_low) as low_samples count as sample_count min(sample_minute) as window_start by host instance
| eventstats max(sample_minute) as latest_sample by host instance
| where sample_minute=latest_sample AND sample_count=3 AND low_samples=3 AND sample_minute-window_start<=120
| table latest_sample host instance free_pct used_pct severity low_samples

dataModelAcceleration: The Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows documents `Perfmon:LogicalDisk` and `PerfmonMk:LogicalDisk` as mapping to the CIM `Performance` model. Before using the optional query, verify that the installed add-on and local tags populate `Performance.dest`, `Performance.mount`, and `Performance.storage_free_percent` for the exact source type, then accelerate `Performance.Storage` with a summary range longer than the ten-minute search window. The CIM variant intentionally uses percentage only; the raw event search remains authoritative for `Free Megabytes`, counter-pair completeness, and event provenance. Do not use the former fictitious `Performance.host` field or assume that an unverified `storage_used_percent` alias is present.

knownFalsePositives:
The detector reports genuine low free capacity in the collected counter; the cases below are expected or mis-scoped conditions that can make paging inappropriate, not proof that the value is false.

1. **Approved patching, feature upgrade, or installer cache growth** — Windows Update, component servicing, and an application installer can temporarily consume the system volume. Match the host, deployment/change record, expected reclaim step, and end time. Keep the finding visible until free capacity actually recovers.

2. **Backup, VSS, database, or log-maintenance window** — Shadow-copy growth, local backup staging, database backup files, transaction logs, or dump creation can be intentional. Confirm the exact volume and owning job; repeated failure to reclaim remains actionable.

3. **Ephemeral cloud temporary disk or disposable build volume** — A short-lived volume may be allowed to fill by design. Suppress only a stable asset/volume identity with an accountable owner. A drive letter alone is insufficient because letters can be reused after reconfiguration.

4. **Recovery, OEM, optical, removable, cluster, or mount-point instance** — The input can enumerate non-application volumes. Verify the instance with Windows Disk Management, `Get-Volume`, and the service inventory. Do not globally exclude `_Total` alternatives such as `HarddiskVolume*`; valid mounted folders can have non-letter identities.

5. **Volume expansion or mount remapping in progress** — Counter values and instance labels can change during an approved storage operation. Confirm the post-change volume identity and three fresh paired samples before closing the finding.

6. **Duplicate collection paths** — Two deployment apps or local and remote Perfmon inputs can emit duplicate values. Compare `_raw`, `source`, `host`, stanza ownership, and `_indextime`, then remove the overlap rather than masking it with `dedup`.

If notification suppression is allowed, use a reviewed `windows_disk_capacity_exceptions.csv` keyed by an immutable asset identifier plus exact `instance`, UTC `start_epoch`, UTC `end_epoch`, `owner`, `ticket`, and `reason`. Reject wildcards and non-expiring rows, apply the lookup after measurement, and publish suppressed findings to a review panel. The base SPL intentionally contains no lookup so an absent or malformed exception file cannot hide a full volume.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement contract

Assign a Windows platform owner, a Splunk collection owner, a search-content owner, and an escalation owner for every in-scope server. Install a currently supported Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) on the Windows Universal Forwarders used for local collection and make its parsing and search-time knowledge available on the Splunk tiers required by the deployment topology. Splunkbase currently describes the add-on as Splunk-supported and CIM-aware, but this documentation review did not install it or validate a specific Windows, add-on, forwarder, Splunk Enterprise, or Splunk Cloud combination. Check the current compatibility listing and test upgrades outside production, especially when crossing the add-on's documented 5.0.0 breaking-change boundary.

Use local Perfmon collection. Splunk documents that the local input runs through `splunk-perfmon.exe` and Windows' Performance Data Helper API. The forwarder service needs normal permission to query the local counters and send data to the receiving tier; this use case does not justify domain-administrator rights, remote WMI credentials, filesystem deletion rights, volume-resize rights, or unrestricted PowerShell. The search role needs read access to the selected event index and permission to save and schedule this alert. Keep alert-action and add-on administration rights separate.

Define the signal before deploying it. Microsoft documents `LogicalDisk` as the per-logical-partition or per-mount-point object. `% Free Space` is percentage points of total usable space that remain free, so `14.5` means 14.5 percent free and 85.5 percent used; it is not a fraction and must not be multiplied by 100. `Free Megabytes` is the unallocated amount reported in megabytes. Preserve that source unit in search results instead of relabeling it as bytes, GB, or GiB. The two counters describe capacity, not file ownership, physical media health, latency, SAN pool reserve, or cloud quota. `_Total` is an aggregate instance and can conceal one full volume behind another spacious volume, so the alert excludes it and requires each real instance.

The 15, 10, and 5 percent free boundaries in this catalogue are operational starting points for warning, high, and critical. Microsoft and Splunk define the counters but do not mandate those alert thresholds. Review them by workload, volume size, growth rate, recovery lead time, and business impact. A percentage-only policy can alert early on a huge volume with abundant bytes, while a universal absolute threshold can misclassify a tiny recovery volume. This baseline reports `free_mb` for triage and uses percentage for severity; add a separately reviewed absolute-capacity policy only when the estate can define it consistently. The comparisons are strict: exactly 15.0 is normal, exactly 10.0 is warning, and exactly 5.0 is high.

## Step 1 — Configure and verify LogicalDisk collection

Do not edit `Splunk_TA_windows/default/inputs.conf`; add only the reviewed override to `Splunk_TA_windows/local/inputs.conf` in the deployment app. The following event-index configuration intentionally fixes the output shape used by the SPL:

```ini
[perfmon://LogicalDisk]
object = LogicalDisk
counters = % Free Space;Free Megabytes
instances = *
interval = 60
mode = single
useEnglishOnly = true
index = perfmon
disabled = 0
```

`instances=*` asks the API for the available LogicalDisk instances. Keep it so drive letters and mounted folders are discoverable; remove only an exact instance through a reviewed deployment policy. `useEnglishOnly=true` makes the configured English object and counter names portable across supported Windows display locales, but Splunk documents caveats for English-only PDH calls, so test representative localized hosts. `interval=60` supplies the one-minute cadence assumed by the persistence gate. `mode=single` gives one counter/instance value per event and the `Perfmon:LogicalDisk` source type expected by this search. This is an event-index design. Splunk also supports a metrics-index path, and Splunk Lantern uses metric name `LogicalDisk.%_Free_Space`; do not point the event SPL at a metrics index or mix `PerfmonMetrics:LogicalDisk` ITSI examples into this contract.

`index=perfmon` is a catalogue convention, not a Splunk-reserved name. Create and secure it or replace the index consistently in the input, saved search, role, retention policy, and validation searches. Deploy the app through the normal configuration-management path and restart the forwarder if the effective input change requires it. Verify stanza precedence on a representative host with `splunk btool inputs list perfmon://LogicalDisk --debug`; confirm one owning app, both counters, interval 60, single mode, and the intended index.

At each poll, expected raw volume is approximately two events per enumerated instance per host: one percentage and one megabyte value. `_Total` may also be collected but is rejected by the alert. Validate the shape with:

```spl
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:LogicalDisk" earliest=-15m
| stats count values(object) as objects values(counter) as counters values(instance) as instances min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen by host
```

Then inspect several raw events. Required search-time fields are `host`, `counter`, `instance`, and numeric `Value`; `object` should identify `LogicalDisk`. Build a separate source-health report that compares expected Windows assets with `max(_time)` and reports missing hosts and instances. Zero low-space results cannot distinguish healthy storage from an input that stopped.

## Step 2 — Create, understand, and schedule the alert

Save the primary SPL as `UC-1.2.3 - Windows LogicalDisk Free Capacity`. Run it every five minutes on a staggered cron such as `2-57/5 * * * *`, trigger when result count is greater than zero, and throttle by `host,instance` for 30 minutes or until the platform's incident lifecycle owns deduplication. The embedded `earliest=-10m@m latest=-2m@m` leaves two minutes for ordinary forwarding/indexing delay while providing enough history for three one-minute samples. Replace that delay only from measured `_indextime-_time`; preserve completed windows and the three-sample span check.

```spl
index=perfmon sourcetype="Perfmon:LogicalDisk" counter IN ("% Free Space","Free Megabytes") earliest=-10m@m latest=-2m@m
| where isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(instance) AND instance!="_Total"
| eval sample_minute=_time-(_time%60), numeric_value=tonumber(Value)
| where isnotnull(numeric_value)
| eval free_pct_value=if(counter="% Free Space",numeric_value,null()), free_mb_value=if(counter="Free Megabytes",numeric_value,null())
| stats latest(free_pct_value) as free_pct latest(free_mb_value) as free_mb by host instance sample_minute
| where isnotnull(free_pct) AND isnotnull(free_mb) AND free_pct>=0 AND free_pct<=100 AND free_mb>=0
| eval used_pct=round(100-free_pct,2), severity=case(free_pct<5,"critical",free_pct<10,"high",free_pct<15,"warning",true(),"normal"), is_low=if(severity!="normal",1,0)
| sort 0 host instance sample_minute
| streamstats window=3 sum(is_low) as low_samples count as sample_count min(sample_minute) as window_start by host instance
| eventstats max(sample_minute) as latest_sample by host instance
| where sample_minute=latest_sample AND sample_count=3 AND low_samples=3 AND sample_minute-window_start<=120
| eval free_pct=round(free_pct,2), free_mb=round(free_mb,0)
| table latest_sample host instance free_pct used_pct free_mb severity low_samples
| sort 0 severity free_pct host instance
```

### Understanding this SPL

The base search selects only the two exact English counters from the event source type and applies fixed event-time bounds. The first `where` rejects missing identities and `_Total`; it does not discard non-letter mount points. `sample_minute` floors `_time` to a 60-second bucket, and `tonumber(Value)` prevents lexical comparisons. The conditional fields separate percentage and megabyte events. `stats latest()` then pairs the newest value of each counter for the same host, instance, and minute. The next `where` is a data-quality firewall: an alert requires both counters, percentage from 0 through 100, and nonnegative free megabytes.

`used_pct` is derived as `100-free_pct`; it is not read from an unrelated counter. `case` applies strict free-percentage boundaries and `is_low` makes warning, high, and critical all count toward persistence. After deterministic ascending order, `streamstats window=3` evaluates each volume's last three complete paired samples. The result must have three low samples and span no more than 120 seconds, so three old values separated by a missing minute do not masquerade as continuous pressure. `eventstats` and the latest-sample filter produce at most one current row per host-volume in a dispatch. The output keeps the native free-megabyte unit and does not infer total capacity by dividing two rounded counters.

For a CIM acceleration path, first prove the add-on's `Perfmon:LogicalDisk` events enter `Performance.Storage` and populate `dest`, `mount`, and `storage_free_percent`. Then use the `cimSpl` in this sidecar. It reproduces the percentage persistence logic over one-minute summaries. It cannot enforce the raw two-counter pair or return authoritative `Free Megabytes`, so keep the event search as the production alert unless the normalized contract is separately validated. Accelerating a model does not create missing tags or fields.

## Step 3 — Validate values, boundaries, timing, and coverage

On one representative host from each supported Windows/add-on family, open Windows Performance Monitor and add `\LogicalDisk(*)\% Free Space` and `\LogicalDisk(*)\Free Megabytes`, or run PowerShell `Get-Counter` against those exact paths. Compare `C:`, a data volume, and a mounted-folder or non-letter instance when present with same-time raw Splunk events. Allow only collection-time and documented Perfmon rounding differences. Confirm that the Splunk `host` is the monitored Windows host, `instance` matches the native instance, `counter` uses the exact English label, percentage remains in 0-100 percentage points, and free capacity remains in megabytes.

Execute the positive and negative `controlTest` fixtures in an isolated index or with `makeresults`-constructed rows, then append the pipeline beginning at the first `where`. The positive must yield one latest critical `C:` row. The negative must yield none. Add explicit unit tests for 15.0, 10.0, and 5.0: expected labels are normal, warning, and high because the comparisons are strict. Values just below those points should be warning, high, and critical. Test `Value="not-a-number"`, percentage above 100, negative megabytes, a missing counter partner, `_Total`, a duplicate event in one minute, and a three-sample sequence with a minute gap. Retain the exact fixtures and outputs when SPL changes.

For safe end-to-end validation, use a non-production volume and a change record. Prefer a reversible, bounded test file or a temporary expandable virtual disk; calculate the requested size, maintain enough recovery headroom, and have console access and a cleanup plan. Do not fill a production system or database volume. Compare the alert's free percentage and megabytes with Performance Monitor before, during, and after cleanup, and verify the incident closes only after three healthy fresh samples if the local lifecycle uses recovery persistence.

Check dispatch history for several cycles. Confirm the search has no peer errors, adjacent schedules complete, and data delay fits inside two minutes. Separately reconcile hosts against the Windows inventory and instances against `Get-Volume` or Disk Management. During this editorial review, no forwarder was configured, no Windows volume was filled, no SPL ran on a Splunk platform, and no CIM acceleration was inspected. Keep `status=draft` until an accountable Windows/Splunk owner completes those checks.

## Step 4 — Operationalize response, dashboards, and evidence

Implement the panels in `visualization` with a default 24-hour operations range and a seven-day capacity-review range. Restrict raw Perfmon access and alert editing to the appropriate platform roles; host and volume labels can expose system architecture and tenant naming. Show source age and exception state beside every capacity row. Use a separate expected-source panel rather than converting missing telemetry into a zero-capacity alert.

Route warning to the owning service queue, high to Windows/storage operations, and critical to the production on-call according to business tier. A critical result means less than 5 percent free for three paired samples; it does not prove an outage or identify the consumer. The runbook should verify the native counter, volume identity, current source age, and active change; inspect `Get-Volume`, Disk Management, application/database logs, VSS usage, backup staging, crash dumps, update caches, and growth history; identify the owner; and select a reversible remediation. Do not automate file deletion, VSS removal, database-log truncation, compression, quota changes, or volume expansion from this signal alone.

When a volume is expected to grow, estimate time-to-exhaustion in a separately validated forecast using longer history; do not overload this three-sample alert with `predict`. For cluster shared volumes, cloud temporary disks, mount points, and database volumes, document the service-specific response and whether drive letters are stable. After a resize or remount, verify new raw instance identity and update only exact inventory or exception keys.

For each deployment and alert revision, retain the artifacts listed in `evidence`, including the native comparison and source-coverage reconciliation. Record threshold rationale, owners, exception approvals, dispatch delay, throttle key, control outputs, and a hash or version of the search. Apply local retention policy; a dashboard screenshot without raw samples, saved-search configuration, and coverage evidence is insufficient to reconstruct the control.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and suppress safely

- **No `Perfmon:LogicalDisk` events:** confirm the add-on is installed on the Windows collection tier, the local stanza is enabled, the effective app path and index exist, the forwarder restarted when required, and `splunk-perfmon.exe` has no input error. Use `btool --debug` to find a higher-precedence disabled stanza.
- **Only `_Total` appears:** inspect `instances` in the effective input and enumerate native paths with `Get-Counter -ListSet LogicalDisk`. Do not alert on `_Total`; restore per-instance collection because an aggregate can hide a full volume.
- **Counters are absent or translated:** verify exact `object=LogicalDisk`, both counter names, and `useEnglishOnly=true`. On a localized or unsupported host, test PDH English-counter availability rather than renaming the SPL to one machine's display language.
- **`Value` or identity fields are null:** confirm `mode=single`, `sourcetype=Perfmon:LogicalDisk`, and add-on search-time knowledge on the search tier. Do not use `PerfmonMk:LogicalDisk` or `PerfmonMetrics:LogicalDisk` with this event-field contract without a separately tested query.
- **Percentage exists but megabytes do not:** verify `Free Megabytes` is in the effective counter list and inspect raw events. The search intentionally rejects an incomplete pair; do not manufacture absolute free capacity from an unrelated volume-size lookup.
- **A valid mounted folder disappears:** remove any local blanket `HarddiskVolume*` or drive-letter-only filter, then reconcile `instance` with Performance Monitor and `Get-Volume`. Keep exact stable identities in policy.
- **Rows duplicate:** locate overlapping deployment apps, duplicate stanzas, remote WMI collection, or reindexed data using `_raw`, `source`, `_indextime`, and configuration precedence. Fix collection ownership rather than adding broad `dedup`.
- **The alert is late or misses persistence:** measure `_indextime-_time`, confirm 60-second polling, inspect forwarder queues and host time, and review minute buckets. Increase dispatch delay from evidence; do not loosen the 120-second continuity check silently.
- **CIM query returns no data:** verify tags, dataset membership, prefixed `Performance.dest`, `Performance.mount`, and `Performance.storage_free_percent`, plus acceleration status and summary range. Use `summariesonly=f` during diagnosis only; return to the raw event alert if normalization is incomplete.
- **Expected maintenance pages:** apply only the exact, expiring exception process in `knownFalsePositives`. Preserve suppressed rows for review and never create a permanent host-wide exception merely because a server has one disposable volume.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how much room remains on every Windows drive and wait for several low readings before warning the team. That gives people time to clean up or add space before a full drive stops important work.

cost.search_load_notes: Five-minute scheduled aggregation over ten minutes of two one-minute LogicalDisk counters; no joins, subsearches, or real-time search.
